title: Readiness vignette: stress simulation & KPI journal
body:
Purpose:
This is a working notebook for structured "vignette" simulations we run before major product rollouts. Goal: translate qualitative worries (e.g., ‘what if caching thrashes under spike?’) into concrete KPIs, thresholds, and quick-play runbooks that product ops, SRE, and product owners can exercise in a 60–90m tabletop.

Context & assumptions:
- Target feature: staged traffic shift to Redwood Hosted API + Dedicated fallback.
- Primary metrics: p50/p95 latency (in ms), tokens/sec throughput, cost per 1k tokens, error rate (5xx), success rate for quality eval prompts (QA pass %), KV cache hit rate.
- Data sources: Console traces, per-route token billing, model quality eval harness (evals), synthetic canary traffic generator, and SLO dashboard (Datadog + internal telemetry).
- Constraint: canary windows are 30m by default; capacity autoscale delay ~4m; batch latency increases with queue depth.

Quick checklist (pre-sim):
- [ ] Confirm canary dataset and 6 golden prompts uploaded (Confluence link above).
- [ ] Notify SRE + infra-on-call calendar slot 14:00-15:30 (owner: Mate o Cruz).
- [ ] Ensure fallback model variants are pinned and tested (prod tag v1.7f-fallback).
- [ ] Synthetic generator runbook accessible and secrets present.

Vignette A: Sudden traffic spike from marketing campaign (10x baseline for 20m)
- Expected system response: queue depth increases, batching improves cost, but tail latency may spike; autoscale may lag.
- KPIs to watch (primary): p95 latency > 1200ms, error rate > 1.5%
- Secondary: KV cache hit rate drop > 15 p.p., tokens/sec per GPU saturation > 85%
- Threshold triggers and actions:
  * If p95 > 1200ms for two consecutive 5m windows -> escalate to SRE and flip to conservative batching (reduce max batch size) and increase dedicated capacity pool (manual burst) -> comms: "Traffic spike: enabling conservative batching; scaling dedicated pool"
  * If error rate > 1.5% -> immediate rollback of recent prompt template change + reroute to fallback model variant
- Observability checks: load heatmap, kernel selection logs, batch size histogram, queue depth series.
- Postmortem focus areas: autoscale latency, batching policy, circuit-breaker thresholds.

Vignette B: Model quality regression (new model variant shows lower eval pass on golden prompts)
- Detection: automated evals show QA pass drop >= 6% within canary window or manual reports from pilot users.
- KPIs: golden-prompt pass %, user-reported NPS delta, hallucination rate (manual tagging).
- Actions:
  * If QA pass drops >= 6% -> pause rollout, rollback to previous model, trigger model-review meeting (research + product)
  * If hallucination rate increases but latency and error rates normal -> activate focused canary with stricter reranking threshold + enable more aggressive prompt-safety filters
- Communications template (short): "Model regression detected in canary: pausing rollout and rolling back to stable variant. Investigation started (owner: Priya Nair)."

Vignette C: Regional outage (one region N->2 unreachable)
- Expected impact: Traffic routed to adjacent region -> increased latency and error rate for region-bound customers.
- KPIs: region-specific p50/p95, cross-region error rate, routing fallback percentage, cost delta for cross-region egress.
- Actions:
  * If region p95 increases > 30% and error rate > 2% -> engage network SRE, open emergency routing rule to limit new sessions, apply sticky routing to unaffected region for existing sessions only
  * Communicate to affected customers via status page and account team (customer-success owner assigned)

Canary ramp schedule (recommended):
- t0: 0.5% traffic, 10m observation
- t1: 2% traffic, 20m observation
- t2: 10% traffic, 30m observation
- t3: 30% traffic, 40m observation (fast-fail thresholds tightened)
- t4: 100% (only after 2 consecutive stable 30m windows at t3)
- Notes: for model changes that affect output content, require full-eval pass at each step, not just infra SLOs.

KPI watchlist (with guardrails):
- Performance: p50 < 220ms, p95 < 800ms (hosted typical), p95 target for Dedicated customers per SLA (configurable)
- Reliability: error rate < 0.5% overall, regional error < 1.0%
- Quality: golden-prompt pass >= 92% during canary (for major model upgrades)
- Cost: delta cost per 1k tokens < +20% baseline; if > +30% -> require finance signoff

Escalation matrix (short):
- Severity 1 (service impacting): product-ops PM -> SRE lead -> Eng director -> exec on-call. Immediate incident channel + status page update within 15m.
- Severity 2 (quality/regression): product owner + research -> rollback/mitigation within 30m.

Playbook snippets (copyable):
- Rollback command (infra): "rwh rollback --service=redwood-hosted --model=stable-v1.6 --reason='canary regression'"
- Canary abort comms: "Aborting canary: observed [metric]. Rolling back to stable variant. Next update in 30m."

Experiment log (fields we capture during tabletop):
- simulation_id, vignette, start_ts, end_ts, baseline_metrics_snapshot, canary_metrics_snapshot, trigger_fired, actions_taken, owners, notes
- TODO: make a small sheet to capture this automatically from runbook-run results (owner: Eloise Zhang)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we standardize default canary durations across all product teams? (pros: consistency; cons: some models need longer context to surface regressions)
- Need clearer cost thresholds for Dedicated customers vs Hosted free-tier. Finance input required.
- Validate that the synthetic generator simulates KV cache misses realistically (follow-up with applied-ml).

Appendix: quick reference links and commands
- Synthetic generator: repo/generator/README
- Eval harness: evals/golden-prompts/v1/README
- Observability dashboard: Datadog > Product Ops > Canary SLOs
- Incident template (status page): Confluence - incident-templates/status-page-draft

Notes to self (fragile/working):
- Keep language short in comms, always include owner + ETA.
- Consider adding a short checklist card in Redwood Console UI for product owners when they create a rollout (quick-links to this notebook + canary toggle).
- This doc is deliberately lightweight; capture full postmortems in product-ops/postmortems directory.

End of vignette journal (working).
